input.description: Find admin user actions and page conventions
input.prompt:
I'm reviewing the page at src/app/footy/admin/user/[email]/page.tsx and its component src/components/AdminUserData/AdminUserData.tsx in a Next.js + Mantine app (next-www-toastboy, a football league admin system). Right now this page just shows a Title with the user's name and a raw JSON dump of the entire user object via Mantine's CodeHighlight component, wrapped in Container > Paper > Center.

I need to know:
1. Are there existing server actions in src/actions/auth.ts (or similar) for admin user operations — e.g. changing a user's role, banning/unbanning, verifying email, deleting a user, resending verification? List their names and signatures.
2. Are there other admin pages in src/app/footy/admin/** (e.g. AdminUserList, AdminPlayerList, NewPlayerForm) that show the UI conventions used for "admin actions" — buttons, menus, badges, confirmation dialogs — so I can tell what "logically grouped, clearly labelled admin actions" looks like elsewhere in this codebase?
3. Does AdminUserData.tsx or the admin user list page link to this single-user page — i.e., is this page reachable via a "view details" action from a list, and what did the previous/git-history version of AdminUserData.tsx look like before it became a raw JSON dump (check git log -p on that file to see if it regressed or was always just a debug view)?
4. Is there a FootyChannel.Users broadcast/revalidatePath wired up correctly for actions that would touch this user (per project convention every mutating server action must revalidatePath + broadcast, and every page showing mutable data must render <AutoRefresh channels=... />)?

Report back concisely: whether this single-user admin page currently exposes any admin actions at all (buttons/menus for role change, ban, delete, etc.), what the JSON dump is for (debugging surface vs. deliberate design), and what UI patterns (buttons, Menu, Modal, Badge) are used in sibling admin components like AdminUserList / AdminPlayerList / NewPlayerForm so I can judge whether SYS-560's checklist item "Admin actions are clearly labelled and logically grouped" is currently satisfied or not.
